phase_name: Demonstrate the fix under real concurrency

objectives.description: Build disposable scratch repo with shipped task-lock.sh and git-commit-scoped.sh
Baseline (control): 30 iterations bare add+commit, record misattribution
Path-scoping only: 30 iterations, record misattribution and index.lock failure rate
Full fix: 30 iterations git-commit-scoped.sh, record misattribution and failure rate
Scale to 8 concurrent committers, record failure rate and worst-case wait
Assert V3 and V2 safety gates under concurrency
Assert honest-index-rows addendum renders under concurrency
Confirm no mutex directory leaked after all runs
Record three-arm comparison in implementation summary

verification: Three-arm comparison (30 iterations each, two concurrent committers on disjoint paths): baseline (bare git add + bare git commit) reproduced misattribution 1/30 (contention on git's own index.lock suppresses much of the rest into lock failures rather than clean sweeps, an honest nuance recorded in the summary); path-scoping-only 0/30 misattribution but 10/30 (~33%) index.lock commit-failure rate, confirming the research's predicted regression; full fix (git-commit-scoped.sh) 0/30 misattribution AND 0/30 failure rate. 8-concurrent-committer scale run completed in 0.48s wall-clock with 0/8 warnings/errors and 8 distinct successful commits. Both safety gates (V3 exclude-only refusal, V2 unmatched-path drop) fired correctly under concurrent load without disrupting the concurrent sibling commit. honest-index-rows addendum rendered correctly. No .commit-lock or .scope-lock directory leaked after any run. Scratch repo and test scripts destroyed after the run; stop condition (full-fix arm not materially better than path-scoping-only) did not trigger.
